questions.explanation:
Option A :

- (Oxalate) is a bidentate ligand. It always binds through its two oxygen atoms.

- (Nitrite) is an ambidentate ligand. It can coordinate either through nitrogen or oxygen.

- (Thiocyanate) can also bind through either nitrogen or sulfur, making it an ambidentate ligand.

Option B :

- (Oxalate) as mentioned earlier, is a bidentate ligand.

- Ethylene diamine (en) is also a bidentate ligand, as it always binds through its two nitrogen atoms.

- (Water) is a monodentate ligand, binding only through one oxygen atom.

Option C :

- as mentioned, is an ambidentate ligand.

- as mentioned, is a bidentate ligand.

- is a hexadentate ligand. It always binds through six donor atoms and is not ambidentate.

Option D :

- as mentioned, is a hexadentate ligand.

- as mentioned, is an ambidentate ligand.

- as mentioned, is a bidentate ligand.
